logbook.speaker: Keeper's Log
logbook.text: The ledger is open to the last filled page. The handwriting is Edith Vane's — the keeper who was here before you. It gets smaller toward the bottom, as if she were running out of nerve, not paper.

logbook_2.speaker: Edith Vane
logbook_2.text: "Third night of fog. There is a light off the north rocks that answers mine. It is not the buoy. It is not a ship. It keeps my rhythm — three flashes, then dark — and I have told no one because there is no one out there to tell."

logbook_choice1.text: You close your eyes. The lamp above you is cold and dead.

choices.text: She was tired and seeing things.

logbook_skeptic.text: Fog does strange work on a person alone. You want that to be all this is. The page underneath disagrees.

logbook_believer.text: You look toward the north window. Nothing but grey. But you believe her, and that costs you something you can't name yet.

logbook_merge.speaker: Edith Vane
logbook_merge.text: "If it answers again tonight, I am going to row out and meet it. I will relight the lamp first so whoever comes next can find the way back. Forgive the mess. — E.V."

logbook_choice2.text: That was eleven days ago. The dinghy is gone from the boathouse.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself for now.

logbook_end_radio.text: You should raise Tom on the radio. He ran her last supply out here; he'll want to know.

logbook_end_quiet.text: You'll keep this between you and the ledger. First the lamp. Then the water.

radio.speaker: Radio — Tom Salish
radio.text: The set crackles, then finds a voice. "Marrow light, this is Salish on the mainland. Took you long enough to switch that on. You settling in okay out there?"

radio_2.speaker: Tom Salish
radio_2.text: "Weather's turning by the weekend. I'll run your next supply Thursday if the water lets me."

radio_edith.speaker: Tom Salish
radio_edith.text: The line goes quiet a moment. "...Edith. Yeah. I ran her last supply out and she wouldn't come to the dock. Just waved from the gallery. You find anything in that logbook, you tell me first. Not the county. Me."

radio_checkin.speaker: Tom Salish
radio_checkin.text: "Good. Keep the light steady and the kettle on. Salish out." The static folds back over his voice like fog over a shoreline.

door.text: The spiral stair climbs into the dark toward the lamp room. The great light is dead — no oil, no spark, no reason it should have gone out. Until you relight it, the water past the rocks stays invisible. (The lamp room is the next chapter.)
